items.name: Tomorrow's Headline
items.purpose: Two advance editions describe incompatible outcomes of the coming registration demonstration. Telegraph custody and direct witnesses can separate observation from an editorial certainty.
invariants: Acquired evidence is not complete Truth.
No generic prophecy, mind control or corporate monster kill.
Past circulation, injury and exclusion cannot be erased by late settlement.
generationEnvelope: Ordinary descriptions only; fixed evidence, deadlines, power and rights cannot be invented.

canon.entry: After the opening Breach, accept an independent consented mandate.
canon.truth: P7_PRIVATE_HEADLINE: incompatible advance editions encourage premature administrative closure. Repetition anchors institutional belief, not universal physical Truth. The surviving pre-Settlement draft contradicts later claims of complete registration.
stakes: On day fourteen an unchecked definitive edition becomes the default administrative account; correction remains possible but cannot erase its circulation.
Protect current people while retaining incompatible evidence.

interventions: Obtain consent for attributed reporting and protect witness copies before publication.
consequences: Corrections and minority accounts remain visible. Sources face attention.
Witness custody protected. Competitors may set the narrative.
Documented access and correction route. Gatekeepers retain information power.
Copies remain available. Premature certainty can acquire institutional force.

sources.text: The press custodian provides dated contradictory drafts, including an old preliminary Eastbank list marked incomplete before a later edition called it final.
Separate observers retain incompatible advance claims as claims, not witnessed events. Their controlled account records continuing address discrepancies at the demonstration site.
A telegraph duplicate places the earlier incomplete-list report before the official final account; transmission order is independently verifiable.
A consented present-site comparison finds two posted identity schedules still producing incompatible admissions. Newspaper repetition has not removed that observable conflict.
